note:
Re-measured 2026-09-14 after the moderation v7 corpus retrain was adopted at threshold 0.80. **Both the rows and a detector changed in this entry, so no rate here is comparable with the one above it.** rows_content_sha256 moved from 7e0dfa86848b to 6864838498d9 because ordinary_rows draws its corpus half from the moderation corpus mundane_* registers, and regenerating that corpus re-drew them. The row set is also better than it was: the v7 corpus carries five mundane registers where v5 carried four, so the sweep now includes enterprise prose, which is the register the retrain was generated to fix. That is the third distinct reason this file has been rewritten, after a sampling artifact and a deliberate behaviour change, and the row hash is what tells the three apart.

What must not be read out of the comparison: pii reads 0.2436 against 0.2521 and is now under its 0.25 ceiling, so its strict xfail XPASSed and it moves into MAX_FIRE_RATE. That is the row set, not the detector. pii is unchanged in this entry, the margin is one row of 234, and two ordinary rows carrying a name would put it back over. Read it as newly enforced rather than as newly fixed.

What is attributable to the retrain, because it is the only detector whose weights moved: moderation fires on 0.0769 against 0.0983, having been given a ceiling of 0.10 in the same commit. It had no entry in MAX_FIRE_RATE or KNOWN_OVER at all until then, so its rate was guarded by nothing, and neither was topic_scope's. over_ceiling iterates the ceilings rather than the measured detectors, so a detector in neither dict is silently unguarded; a completeness test now fails if one is.

See _SEGMENTED in detectors/classifier.py for the per-detector segmentation table. moderation stays in it: the v7 corpus removed the length imbalance it was generated to remove and the padding evasion did not move, 52/60 to 54/60 by suffix with segmentation off, so the corpus was not the cause and the segment pass is load-bearing rather than a stopgap.

The moderation artifact changed again later the same day, to the int8-fp16 hybrid, 364 MB against the int8 export's 535, and no rate in this file moved. Not within tolerance: identical, all eleven detectors over the same 234 rows on both sides. The file is therefore left as measured rather than regenerated, and this paragraph is the record that it was re-measured rather than assumed. RATE_TOLERANCE is sized so that a model swap fails this comparison, so a swap that changes nothing is a result about the export and not a gap in the check.
